paragraphs.sourceText: Why would an animal kill itself? It seems a strange question, and yet it is one that has 26 some people for a long time. The lemming (旅鼠) is one such animal. Lemmings periodically commit mass 27 , and no one knows just why!

The small 28 , which inhabit the Scandinavian mountains, sustain themselves on a diet of roots and live in nests they make underground. When their food supply is 29 large, the lemmings live a normal, undisturbed life.

However, when the lemmings' food supply becomes too low to support the population, a singular 30 commences. The lemmings leave their nests all together at the same time, forming huge crowds. Great numbers of the lemmings begin a long and hard journey across the Scandinavian plains, z journey that may last weeks. The lemmings eat everything in their path, continuing their 31 march until they reach the sea.

The reason for what follows remains a mystery for zoologists and naturalists. Upon reaching the coast, the lemmings do not stop but swim by the thousands into the surf. Most 32 only a short time before they tire, sink, and drown.

A common theory for this unusual phenomenon is that the lemmings do not realize that the ocean is such 33 water. In their cross-country journey, the animals must traverse many smaller bodies of water, such as rivers and small lakes. They may 34 that the sea is just another such swimmable
35 . But no final answer has been found to the mystery.
paragraphs.translationZh: 35.但这个谜团尚未找到最终答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: “That which does not kill us makes us stronger. ” But parents can’t handle it when teenagers put this 36 into practice. Now technology has become the new field for the age-old battle between adults and their freedom-seeking kids.

Locked indoors, unable to get on their bicycles and hang out with their friends, teens have turned to social media and their mobile phones to socialize with their peers. What they do online often 37 what they might otherwise do if their mobility weren’t so heavily 38 in the age of helicopter parenting. Social media and smart-phone apps have become so popular in recent years because teens need a place to call their own. They want the freedom to 39 their identity and the world around them. Instead of 40 out, they jump online.

As teens have moved online, parents have projected their fears onto the Internet, imagining all the 41 dangers that youth might face —from 42 strangers to cruel peers to pictures or words that could haunt them on Google for the rest of their lives.

Rather than helping teens develop strategies for negotiating public life and the risks of 43 with others, fearful parents have focused on tracking, monitoring and blocking. These tactics（策略）don‘t help teens develop the skills they need to manage complex social situations, 44 risks and get help when they’re in trouble. “Protecting” kids may fed like the right thing to do, but it 45 the learning that teens need to do as they come of age in a technology-soaked world. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。

paragraphs.sourceText: Inequality Is Not Inevitable
paragraphs.translationZh: 不平等并非不可避免

paragraphs.sourceText: A) A dangerous trend has developed over this past third of a century. A country that experienced shared growth after World War Ⅱbegan to tear apart, so much so that when the Great Recession hit in late 2007，one could no longer ignore the “shining city on a hiir ” become the division that had come to define the American economic landscape. How did this advanced country with the greatest level of inequality?
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 在过去的三分之一个世纪里，一种危险的趋势已经形成。一个在二战后经历过共同增长的国家开始分裂，以至于当2007年底经济大衰退袭来时，人们再也无法忽视“山上的闪亮城市”成为美国经济版图的划分。这个不平等程度最高的发达国家是如何度过的？

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Over the past year and a half, The Great Divide, a series in The New York Times, has presented a wide range of examples that undermine the notion that there are any truly fundamental laws of capitalism. The dynamics of the imperial capitalism of the 19th century needn’ t apply in the democracies of the 21st. We don’t need to have this much inequality in America.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 在过去的一年半里，《纽约时报》的系列文章《大分水岭》提出了各种各样的例子，这些例子破坏了资本主义存在真正基本规律的观念。 19 世纪帝国资本主义的动态不一定适用于 21 世纪的民主国家。美国不需要如此严重的不平等。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Our current brand of capitalism is a fake capitalism. For proof of this go back to our response to the Great Recession, where we socialized losses, even as we privatized gains. Perfect competition should drive profits to zero, at least theoretically, but we have monopolies making persistently high profits. C. E. O. s enjoy incomes that are on average 295 times that of the typical worker, a much higher ratio than in the past, without any evidence of a proportionate increase in productivity.
paragraphs.translationZh: C）我们目前的资本主义品牌是假资本主义。要证明这一点，请回到我们对大衰退的反应，当时我们将损失社会化，即使我们将收益私有化。至少在理论上，完美竞争应该将利润推向零，但我们有垄断企业持续赚取高额利润。 CEO 的平均收入是普通工人的 295 倍，这一比例比过去高得多，但没有任何证据表明生产率相应提高。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) If it is not the cruel laws of economics that have led to America’s great divide, what is it? The straightforward answer： our policies and our politics! People get tired of hearing about Scandinavian success stories, but the fact of the matter is that Sweden, Finland and Norway have all succeeded in having about as much or faster growth in per capita(人均的) incomes than the United States and with far greater equality.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）如果不是残酷的经济规律导致了美国的巨大分裂，那是什么？直接的答案：我们的政策和我们的政治！人们厌倦了听到斯堪的纳维亚的成功故事，但事实是，瑞典、芬兰和挪威都成功地实现了与美国同等或更快的人均收入增长，而且更加平等。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. So why has America chosen these inequality-enhancing policies? Part of the answer is that as World War II faded into memory, so too did the solidarity it had created. As America triumphed in the Cold War，there didn’t seem to be a real competitor to our economic model. Without this international competition, we no longer had to show that our system could deliver for most of our citizens.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 那么，美国为什么选择这些加剧不平等的政策呢？部分答案是，随着第二次世界大战逐渐淡入人们的记忆，它所创造的团结也随之消失。当美国在冷战中取得胜利时，我们的经济模式似乎没有真正的竞争对手。如果没有这种国际竞争，我们就不再需要证明我们的系统可以为大多数公民提供服务。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Ideology and interests combined viciously. Some drew the wrong lesson from the collapse of the Soviet system in 1991. The pendulum swung from much too much government there to much too little here. Corporate interests argued for getting rid of regulations, even when those regulations had done so much to protect and improve our environment, our safety, our health and the economy itself.
paragraphs.translationZh: F）意识形态与利益恶性结合。一些人从 1991 年苏联体制的崩溃中吸取了错误的教训。形势从苏联政府过多转向政府过少。企业利益主张废除法规，即使这些法规在保护和改善我们的环境、安全、健康和经济本身方面发挥了巨大作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) But this ideology was hypocriticail(虚伪的）.The bankers, among the strongest advocates of laissez-faire (自由放任的） economics, were only too willing to accept hundreds of billions of dollars from the government in the aid programs that have been a recurring feature of the global economy since the beginning of the Thatcher-Reagan era of “free” markets and deregulation.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 但这种意识形态是虚伪的。银行家是自由放任经济学的最有力倡导者，他们非常愿意接受政府提供的数千亿美元的援助计划，这些计划自撒切尔-里根“自由”市场和放松管制时代开始以来一直是全球经济的一个反复出现的特征。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) The American political system is overrun by money. Economic inequality translates into political inequality, and political inequality yields increasing economic inequality. So corporate welfare increases as we reduce welfare for the poor. Congress maintains subsidies for rich farmers as we cut back on nutritional support for the needy. Drug companies have been given hundreds of billions of dollars as we limit Medicaid benefits. The banks that brought on the global financial crisis got billions while a tiny bit went to the homeowners and victims of the same banks’ predatory (掠夺性的）lending practices. This last decision was particularly foolish. There were alternatives to throwing money at the banks and hoping it would circulate through increased lending.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 美国的政治体系被金钱所淹没。经济不平等转化为政治不平等，政治不平等又导致经济不平等加剧。因此，当我们减少穷人的福利时，企业福利就会增加。当我们减少对贫困人口的营养支持时，国会仍维持对富裕农民的补贴。由于我们限制医疗补助福利，制药公司已经获得了数千亿美元。引发全球金融危机的银行获得了数十亿美元，而一小部分流向了房主和同一银行掠夺性贷款行为的受害者。最后的决定特别愚蠢。除了向银行扔钱并希望通过增加贷款来循环之外，还有其他选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Our divisions are deep. Economic and geographic segregation has immunized those at the top from the problems of those down below. Like the kings of ancient times, they have come to perceive their privileged positions essentially as a natural right.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 我们的分歧很深。经济和地理上的隔离使上层人士免受下层人士问题的影响。就像古代的国王一样，他们逐渐将自己的特权地位视为一种自然权利。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Our economy, our democracy and our society have paid for these gross inequalities. The true test of an economy is not how much wealth its princes can accumulate in tax havens (庇护所），but how well off the typical citizen is. But average incomes are lower than they were a quarter-century ago. Growth has gone to the very, very top, whose share has almost increased four times since 1980. Money that was meant to have trickled (流淌) down has instead evaporated in the agreeable climate of the Cayman Islands.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 我们的经济、我们的民主和我们的社会已经为这些严重的不平等付出了代价。对一个经济体的真正考验不是王子们能在避税天堂积累多少财富，而是普通公民的生活状况如何。但平均收入比四分之一世纪前要低。经济增长已经到了非常非常顶端，自1980年以来，他们的份额几乎增加了四倍。本来应该流淌下来的钱，在开曼群岛宜人的气候中却蒸发了。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) With almost a quarter of American children younger than 5 living in poverty, and with America doing so little for its poor, the deprivations of one generation are being visited upon the next. Of course, no country has ever come close to providing complete equality of opportunity. But why is America one of the advanced countries where the life prospects of the young are most sharply determined by the income and education of their parents?
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 由于近四分之一的五岁以下美国儿童生活在贫困之中，而且美国为穷人做的事情又很少，一代人的贫困正在影响到下一代。当然，没有一个国家能够提供完全平等的机会。但为什么美国是年轻人的生活前景最受父母收入和教育程度影响的发达国家之一呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Among most bitter stories in The Great Divide were those that portrayed the frustrations of the young, who long to enter our shrinking middle class. Soaring tuitions and declining incomes have resulted in larger debt burdens. Those with only a high school diploma have seen their incomes decline by 13 percent over the past 35 years.
paragraphs.translationZh: L）《大鸿沟》中最痛苦的故事是那些描绘年轻人的挫败感的故事，他们渴望进入我们日益萎缩的中产阶级。学费飙升和收入下降导致债务负担更大。过去 35 年里，那些只有高中文凭的人的收入下降了 13%。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Where justice is concerned, there is also a huge divide. In the eyes of the rest of the world and a significant part of its own population, mass imprisonment has come to define America—a country, it bears repeating，with about 5 percent of the world’s population but around a fourth of the world’s prisoners.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 在正义方面，也存在着巨大的分歧。在世界其他国家和美国很大一部分人口的眼中，大规模监禁已经成为美国的定义——值得重申的是，美国是一个拥有世界约 5% 人口但囚犯数量约占世界四分之一的国家。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Justice has become a commodity, affordable to only a few. While Wall Street executives used their expensive lawyers to ensure that their ranks were not held accountable for the misdeeds that the crisis in 2008 so graphically revealed, the banks abused our legal system to foreclose (取消赎回权）on mortgages and eject tenants, some of whom did not even owe money.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 正义已成为一种商品，只有少数人才能负担得起。尽管华尔街高管们聘请了昂贵的律师来确保他们的团队不会对 2008 年危机如此生动地揭露的不当行为负责，但银行却滥用我们的法律制度取消抵押贷款赎回权并驱逐租户，其中一些租户甚至不欠钱。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) More than a half-century ago, America led the way in advocating for the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations in 1948. Today, access to health care is among the most universally accepted rights, at least in the advanced countries. America, despite the implementation of the Affordable Care Act, is the exception. In the relief that many felt when the Supreme Court did not overturn the Affordable Care Act, the implications of the decision for Medicaid were not fully appreciated. Obamacare’s objective —to ensure that all Americans have access to health care—has been blocked：24 states have not implemented the expanded Medicaid program, which was the means by which Obamacare was supposed to deliver on its promise to some of the poorest.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 半个多世纪前，美国带头倡导联合国于 1948 年通过的《世界人权宣言》。如今，获得医疗保健已成为最普遍接受的权利之一，至少在发达国家是这样。尽管实施了《平价医疗法案》，美国却是个例外。当最高法院没有推翻《平价医疗法案》时，许多人感到如释重负，但这一决定对医疗补助的影响并没有得到充分认识。奥巴马医改的目标——确保所有美国人都能获得医疗保健——已被阻碍：24个州尚未实施扩大的医疗补助计划，而奥巴马医改本应通过该计划兑现其对一些最贫困人口的承诺。

paragraphs.sourceText: P) We need not just a new war on poverty but a war to protect the middle class. Solutions to these problems do not have to be novel. Far from it. Making markets act like markets would be a good place to start. We must end the rent-seeking society we have gravitated toward, in which the wealthy obtain profits by manipulating the system. Q) The problem of inequality is not so much a matter of technical economics. It’s really a problem of practical politics. Inequality is not just about the top marginal tax rate but also about our children’s access to food and the right to justice for all. If we spent more on education, health and infrastructure (基础设施），we would strengthen our economy, now and in the future. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: P）我们不仅需要一场新的反贫困战争，还需要一场保护中产阶级的战争。这些问题的解决方案不一定是新颖的。远非如此。让市场像市场一样运作将是一个很好的起点。我们必须结束我们所趋向的寻租社会，在这个社会中，富人通过操纵制度来获取利润。问）不平等问题与其说是技术经济学问题。这确实是一个现实政治问题。不平等不仅涉及最高边际税率，还涉及我们的孩子获得食物的机会和所有人获得正义的权利。如果我们在教育、卫生和基础设施（基础设施）上投入更多，我们现在和将来都会加强我们的经济。注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2上作答。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. In theory, free competition is supposed to reduce the margin of profits to the minimum.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 从理论上讲，自由竞争应该将利润率降低到最低限度。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. The United States is now characterized by a great division between the rich and the poor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 美国现在的特点是贫富差距巨大。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. America lacked the incentive to care for the majority of its citizens as it found no rival for its economic model.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 美国缺乏关心其大多数公民的动力，因为它没有发现其经济模式的竞争对手。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. The wealthy top have come to take privileges for granted.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 富有的上层人士已经开始认为特权是理所当然的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Many examples show the basic laws of imperial capitalism no longer apply in present-day America.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 许多例子表明帝国资本主义的基本法则不再适用于当今的美国。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. The author suggests a return to the true spirit of the market.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 作者建议回归市场的真正精神。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. A quarter of the world’s prisoner population is in America.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 世界上四分之一的囚犯在美国。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. Government regulation in America went from one extreme to the other in the past two decades.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 过去二十年里，美国的政府监管从一个极端转向了另一个极端。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. Justice has become so expensive that only a small number of people like corporate executives can afford it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 伸张正义变得如此昂贵，只有企业高管等少数人才能负担得起。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. No country in the world so far has been able to provide completely equal opportunities for all.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 迄今为止，世界上没有一个国家能够为所有人提供完全平等的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: I’ll admit I’ve never quite understood the obsession (难以破除的成见）surrounding genetically modified (GM) crops. To environmentalist opponents, GM foods are simply evil, an understudied, possibly harmful tool used by big agricultural businesses to control global seed markets and crush local farmers. They argue that GM foods have never delivered on their supposed promise, that money spent on GM crops would be better channeled to organic farming and that consumers should be protected with warning labels on any products that contain genetically modified ingredients. To supporters, GM crops are a key part of the effort to sustainably provide food to meet a growing global population. But more than that, supporters see the GM opposition of many environmentalists as fundamentally anti-science, no different than those who question the basics of man-made climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我承认我从来没有完全理解围绕转基因（GM）作物的痴迷（难以破除的成见）。对于环保主义者的反对者来说，转基因食品简直是邪恶的，是大型农业企业用来控制全球种子市场和镇压当地农民的未经充分研究的、可能有害的工具。他们认为转基因食品从未兑现其所谓的承诺，花在转基因作物上的钱将更好地用于有机农业，并且应该在任何含有转基因的产品上贴上警告标签来保护消费者。对于支持者来说，转基因作物是可持续提供粮食以满足不断增长的全球人口的努力的关键部分，但更重要的是，支持者认为许多环保主义者的反对从根本上来说是反科学的，与那些质疑人为气候变化的基本原理的人没有什么不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: For both sides, GM foods seem to act as a symbol：you’re pro-agricultural business or anti-science. But science is exactly what we need more of when it comes to GM foods, which is why I was happy to see Nature devote a special series of articles to the GM food controversy. The conclusion：while GM crops haven’t yet realized their initial promise and have been dominated by agricultural businesses, there is reason to continue to use and develop them to help meet the enormous challenge of sustainably feeding a growing planet.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于双方来说，转基因食品似乎都充当了一种象征：你是支持农业企业还是反对科学。但当谈到转基因食品时，科学正是我们更需要的，这就是为什么我很高兴看到《自然》杂志针对转基因食品争议专门发表了一系列文章。结论：虽然转基因作物尚未实现其最初的承诺，并且一直由农业企业主导，但我们有理由继续使用和开发它们，以帮助应对可持续养活不断增长的地球的巨大挑战。

paragraphs.sourceText: That doesn’t mean GM crops are perfect, or a one-size-fits-all solution to global agriculture problems. But anything that can increase farming efficiency —the amount of crops we can produce per acre of land— will be extremely useful. GM crops can and almost certainly will be part of that suite of tools, but so will traditional plant breeding, improved soil and crop management —and perhaps most important of all, better storage and transport infrastructure(基础设施), especially in the developing world. (It doesn’t do much good for farmers in places like sub-Saharan Africa to produce more food if they can 't get it to hungry consumers.) I 'd like to see more non-industry research done on GM crops—not just because we’d worry less about bias，but also because seed companies like Monsanto and Pioneer shouldn’t be the only entities working to harness genetic modification. Td like to see GM research on less commercial crops, like corn. I don’t think it’s vital to label GM ingredients in food, but I also wouldn’t be against it —and industry would be smart to go along with labeling, just as a way of removing fears about the technology.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这并不意味着转基因作物是完美的，也不意味着它是解决全球农业问题的万能解决方案。但任何能够提高农业效率（每英亩土地可以生产的农作物数量）的东西都将非常有用。转基因作物可以而且几乎肯定会成为这套工具的一部分，但传统的植物育种、改良的土壤和作物管理也将成为这一工具的一部分——也许最重要的是，更好的储存和运输基础设施，特别是在发展中国家。 （如果撒哈拉以南非洲等地的农民无法将食物提供给饥饿的消费者，那么生产更多的食物对他们来说并没有多大好处。）我希望看到对转基因作物进行更多的非行业研究——不仅因为我们不用担心偏见，还因为像孟山都和先锋这样的种子公司不应该是唯一致力于利用基因改造的实体。我希望看到对玉米等经济性较低的作物进行转基因研究。我认为在食品中贴上转基因成分标签并不重要，但我也不会反对——而且行业会明智地附上标签，作为消除对这项技术的恐惧的一种方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most of all, though, I wish a tenth of the energy that’s spent endlessly debating GM crops was focused on those more pressing challenges for global agriculture. There are much bigger battles to fight.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不过，最重要的是，我希望将无休止的转基因作物争论的十分之一的精力集中在全球农业面临的更紧迫的挑战上。还有更大的战斗要打。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Early decision—you apply to one school? and admission is binding—seems like a great choice for nervous applicants. Schools let in a higher percentage of early-decision applicants, which arguably means that you have a better chance of getting in. And if you do, you’re done with the whole agonizing process by December. But what most students and parents don’t realize is that schools have hidden motives for offering early decision.
paragraphs.translationZh: 提前决定——您申请一所学校？而且录取具有约束力——对于紧张的申请者来说似乎是一个不错的选择。学校录取提前录取申请者的比例更高，这可以说意味着你有更好的机会被录取。如果你这样做了，到 12 月你就完成了整个痛苦的过程。但大多数学生和家长没有意识到，学校提供早期录取服务有隐藏的动机。

paragraphs.sourceText: Early decision, since it’s binding, allows schools to fill their classes with qualified students ；it allows admissions committees to select the students that are in particular demand for their college and know those students will come. It also gives schools a higher yield rate, which is often used as one of the ways to measure college selectivity and popularity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 早期决定具有约束力，允许学校在班级中招收合格的学生；它允许招生委员会选择学校特别需要的学生，并知道这些学生会来。它还为学校提供了更高的收益率，这通常被用作衡量大学选择性和受欢迎程度的方法之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: The problem is that this process effectively shortens the window of time students have to make one of the most important decisions of their lives up to that point. Under regular admissions, seniors have until May 1 to choose which school to attend； early decision effectively steals six months from them, months that could be used to visit more schools, do more research, speak to current students and alumni(校友) and arguably make a more informed decision.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题在于，这个过程有效地缩短了学生迄今为止必须做出一生中最重要决定之一的时间。在常规招生下，高年级学生必须在 5 月 1 日之前选择就读哪所学校；提前做出决定实际上会浪费他们六个月的时间，这几个月可以用来参观更多学校、做更多研究、与在校学生和校友交谈，并可以做出更明智的决定。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are, frankly, an astonishing number of exceptional colleges in America, and for any given student, there are a number of schools that are a great fit. When students become too fixated（专注）on a particular school early in the admissions process, that fixation can lead to severe disappointment if they don’t get in or, if they do? the possibility that they are now bound to go to a school that, given time for further reflection, may not actually be right for them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 坦率地说，美国有数量惊人的优秀大学，对于任何特定的学生来说，有许多学校非常适合。当学生在招生过程的早期就过于执着于某所学校时，如果他们没有被录取，这种执着可能会导致严重的失望，或者如果他们被录取了？他们现在可能会去一所学校，如果有时间进一步思考，这所学校可能实际上并不适合他们。

paragraphs.sourceText: Insofar as early decision offers a genuine admissions edge, that advantage goes largely to students who already have numerous advantages. The students who use early decision tend to be those who have received higher-quality college guidance, usually a result of coming from a more privileged background. In this regard，there’s an argument against early decision，as students from lower-income families are far less likely to have the admissions know-how to navigate the often confusing early deadlines.
paragraphs.translationZh: 就早期录取提供真正的录取优势而言，这种优势主要属于已经拥有众多优势的学生。采用早期决策的学生往往是那些接受过更高质量大学指导的学生，这通常是由于来自更优越的背景。在这方面，有人反对提前做出决定，因为来自低收入家庭的学生不太可能拥有招生知识来应对经常令人困惑的提前截止日期。

paragraphs.sourceText: Students who have done their research and are confident that there’s one school they would be thrilled to get into should, under the current system, probably apply under early decision. But for students who haven’t yet done enough research, or who are still constantly changing their minds on favorite schools, the early-decision system needlessly and prematurely narrows the field of possibility just at a time when students should be opening themselves to a whole range of thrilling options. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 在现行制度下，那些已经完成研究并确信有一所他们很高兴能进入的学校的学生可能应该根据早期决定进行申请。但对于尚未做足够研究的学生，或者仍在不断改变对最喜欢的学校的想法的学生来说，早期决策系统不必要地过早地缩小了可能性的范围，而此时学生应该向一系列令人兴奋的选择敞开心扉。
